questions.question_text: Explain the difference between shared-memory and distributed-memory architectures in parallel computing.
questions.answer_key: Shared-memory architecture uses a common memory space accessible by all processors, while distributed-memory architecture uses private memory for each processor, requiring data exchange through communication.

questions.question_text: Apply the concept of Amdahl’s law to evaluate the potential speedup of a parallel algorithm on a MIMD system.
questions.answer_key: Amdahl’s law states that the maximum theoretical speedup that can be achieved by a program is limited by the fraction of the program that cannot be parallelized. To apply this, calculate the speedup using the formula: Speedup = 1 / (1 - P + P/S), where P is the fraction of the program that can be parallelized and S is the number of processors.

questions.question_text: Discuss the importance of coordinating processes/threads in shared-memory and distributed-memory architectures.
questions.answer_key: Coordinating processes/threads is crucial for achieving efficient parallel computation, ensuring data consistency, and preventing race conditions in both shared-memory and distributed-memory architectures.
